# The scoreboard: ISLA against GeoTransolver and Transolver {#sec-scoreboard}

**With every architecture fed the same inputs and scored on the same
float32 instrument, GeoTransolver and Transolver are at least as accurate as
ISLA on every in-distribution surface benchmark measured, by 2% at the
512-wide, 80,000-cell corner and by up to 28% at 35 wing cases; ISLA leads
where geometries arrive in arbitrary poses, on interior velocity, and on
consistency under a change of surface sampling, where its relative frame
degrades 1.2x against 10 to 16x (19x for the weights-off ablation) for
every configuration that centers its coordinates on the sampled points.** This chapter is the standing on one
page. Every cross-architecture measurement of the book appears here,
computed from the same result files the evidence chapters use, so a reader
who needs the standing and not the derivation can stop after this chapter
and go to @sec-data-efficiency, @sec-full-data and @sec-interior only for
the protocol behind a particular row.

## How to read every number {#sec-scoreboard-protocol}

- **The metric** is the area-weighted relative L2 error of surface pressure
  (@sec-metrics), averaged over the validation cases of the split, from a
  float32 inference on the final-epoch checkpoint. Interior rows use the same
  error on interior pressure, velocity and eddy viscosity.
- **The inputs are matched.** Every model receives the freestream as a unit
  direction (the unit-direction protocol, @sec-fair-comparison); tokens per
  case, epochs (500), split and validation cases are identical across
  architectures in every row, and each architecture runs at its own best
  learning rate. GeoTransolver's best rate depends on how much data it sees
  (3e-3 at 200,000 cells on every DrivAerML rung, 1e-3 at 10,000 cells at
  full data); the rows name the rate used.
- **Two budgets, one protocol.** The reporting protocol is the recipe's
  default of 200,000 sampled cells per case (@sec-scoreboard-200k). The
  program explored at 10,000 cells, and every figure and table measured at
  that count carries the label *exploration budget*; on DrivAerML the
  budget changes the standing (parity at 200,000 against an 8% deficit at
  10,000), on the 35-case wing rung it does not.
- **A ratio is baseline error divided by ISLA error**, so a value above one
  favors ISLA. Where a rung was run on several random training draws, the
  ratio carries the 90% interval over draws, which is the uncertainty to read.
- **Which ISLA.** Every ISLA number in this chapter's figures and tables is
  ISLA (relative frame, @sec-mt2; every lane in this chapter was trained
  with the total-measure length unit, within 1.3% of the RMS-pairwise-distance
  default, @sec-nb-lenrms-verdict); the legacy centered variant appears only
  in collapsed diagnostic notes.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="The detail behind those four rules"}
Learning rates: GeoTransolver 3e-3 on the 35-case wing rung and 1e-3
elsewhere; Transolver 3e-3 everywhere; ISLA 1e-3 at width 192 and the width
rule above it (@sec-using-lr). At 1,260 wing cases GeoTransolver and the
legacy centered variant (diagnostic) were also trained at 20,000 cells: each
improves by about 5% and their ratio does not move, so the wing rungs are
not a cell-count floor (@sec-nb-w2c-floor-verdict). ISLA is measured
on eight surface rungs: 35 and 210 wing cases, 4 and 21 training
geometries, the fixed angle, DrivAerML at 435 cars under the independent
and the stratified inference draw, and the corner; the rungs measured only
on the legacy centered variant are listed in @sec-scoreboard-pending, and the
properties first measured on that variant are being re-measured on ISLA
(@sec-nb-refprops-prereg). One further family of
configurations appears where it informs the reading: the baselines with the
surface measure carried in their slice pooling, ablations that
locate a property (GeoTransolver and Transolver are not
modified, @sec-part-baseline).
:::

## Surface pressure: every rung on one axis {#sec-scoreboard-surface}

**At the exploration budget of 10,000 cells the unit-direction baselines
match or beat ISLA on every surface rung; the margin runs from 2% at the
corner to 28% at 35 wing cases and does not close as the training set
grows.** This section is the exploration-budget standing; the reporting
protocol's standing on DrivAerML, where the full-data gap closes to parity,
is @sec-scoreboard-200k, and the 35-case wing rung does not move between
the two budgets (@sec-scoreboard-200k). @fig-scoreboard-forest places every
setting on one axis of baseline error divided by ISLA error; the rows below
the surface rungs are the pose test and the interior task, where ISLA leads.

```{python}
#| label: fig-scoreboard-forest
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The scoreboard on one axis. Each row is one benchmark setting; each
#|   marker is a baseline's surface-pressure error divided by ISLA's on the
#|   same validation cases (GeoTransolver red circles, Transolver amber
#|   triangles), so markers left of the line at 1 favor the baseline and
#|   markers right of it favor ISLA. Every row divides by ISLA and
#|   carries the seed-mean ratio. The bottom rows are the pose test
#|   (baselines trained with rotation augmentation, ISLA without, every case
#|   in a random pose, @sec-nb-poseref-verdict) and the interior task (GeoTransolver-volume
#|   divided by ISLA with query tokens and the signed distance). How to read
#|   this: it shows ratios, not absolute accuracy, and says nothing about
#|   consistency under a change of sampling (@fig-scoreboard-density).
#|   Float32 throughout.
#|   Data: the files listed in @tbl-scoreboard-surface, plus
#|   research/transfer_program/studies/campaign_b_pose/campaign_b_fp32_2026-09-10.json,
#|   results/relint2_reduction_2026-09-14.json and
#|   results/fp32_reeval/fp32_shift_interior_2026-09-09.json.
#| code-fold: true
rows = []  # (label, gt_ratio, t_ratio, filled)
def add(label, key):
    s = S[key]; i = s["isla_ref"]
    rows.append((label, ratio(s["gt"], i), (ratio(s["t"], i) if s["t"] else None), True))
add("HiLift, 35 cases", "hl35")
add("HiLift, 210 cases", "hl210")
add("HiLift, 4 training geometries", "geo4")
add("HiLift, 21 training geometries", "geo21")
add("HiLift, fixed angle 12°", "fixed")
add("DrivAerML, 435 cars", "dr435")
add("DrivAerML, 435 cars, stratified inference draw", "dr435_strat")
add("DrivAerML, 512 wide × 80k cells (width learning rate)", "corner")
n_surface = len(rows)
pB = poseB["arms"]
rows.append(("DrivAerML, every case in a random pose (baselines rotation-augmented)", pB["gt_aug"]["pressure_mean"] / poseR["posed_mean"],
             pB["transolver_aug"]["pressure_mean"] / poseR["posed_mean"], True))
def intf(keys, f): return mean(fp(fpint, keys, f))
gtv = [f"udrv_gt_vol_seed{s}" for s in (42, 43)]; isq = [f"v0_isla_qtsdfval_seed{s}" for s in (42, 43)]  # isq: similarity-gauge interior variant, diagnostic note only
for f, lab in (("pressure_l2", "interior pressure"), ("velocity_l2", "interior velocity"), ("nut_l2", "interior eddy viscosity")):
    rows.append((f"DrivAerML interior, {lab}", ri2["gt_vol_unit"][f]["mean"] / ri2["relint2"][f]["mean"], None, True))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9.6, 5.6))
y = list(range(len(rows)))[::-1]
for yy, (label, rg, rt, filled) in zip(y, rows):
    for r, key, dy in ((rg, "gt", 0.12), (rt, "t", -0.12)):
        if r is None: continue
        c, mk = STYLE[key]["color"], STYLE[key]["marker"]
        ax.plot([r], [yy + dy], marker=mk, ms=8, mfc=(c if filled else "white"), mec=c, mew=1.8, ls="none", zorder=4)
        ax.annotate(f"{r:.2f}", (r, yy + dy), xytext=(0, 7 if dy > 0 else -11), textcoords="offset points", ha="center", fontsize=7.5, color=c)
ax.axvline(1.0, color=INK2, lw=1.2, zorder=1)
ax.axvspan(0.95, 1.05, color=GRID, alpha=0.6, zorder=0)
n_rows = len(rows)
for sep in (n_rows - n_surface - 0.5, n_rows - n_surface - 1.5):  # separate surface rungs / pose / interior
    ax.axhline(sep, color=BASELINE, lw=0.8, ls=":", zorder=1)
ax.set_yticks(y); ax.set_yticklabels([r[0] for r in rows], fontsize=8.5)
ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_xlim(0.62, 1.45)
ax.set_xticks([0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3]); ax.set_xticklabels(["0.7", "0.8", "0.9", "1.0", "1.1", "1.2", "1.3"])
ax.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter())
ax.set_xlabel("baseline error ÷ ISLA error [–]\n(left of 1: the baseline is more accurate; right of 1: ISLA is)")
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
ax.set_ylim(-0.7, y[0] + 0.7)
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
ax.legend(handles=[Line2D([], [], **{k: v for k, v in series_kwargs("gt", ls="none").items() if k in ("color", "marker", "mfc", "mec", "mew", "ms", "ls")}, label="GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA"),
                   Line2D([], [], **{k: v for k, v in series_kwargs("t", ls="none").items() if k in ("color", "marker", "mfc", "mec", "mew", "ms", "ls")}, label="Transolver ÷ ISLA"),
                   mpl.patches.Patch(facecolor=GRID, label="parity within 5%")],
          loc="upper right", fontsize=8, ncol=1)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Every surface marker sits left of one; the pose and interior-velocity
markers sit right of it. The numbers, seeds and paired case counts behind
each marker are in @tbl-scoreboard-surface, and @fig-scoreboard-bars shows
the same rungs as absolute error.

```{python}
#| label: fig-scoreboard-bars
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The surface settings as absolute error. Bars are seed means of the
#|   surface-pressure error (lower is better) for GeoTransolver (red),
#|   Transolver (amber) and ISLA (blue); dots are
#|   the individual seeds. Panels share no vertical scale, since the rungs differ by an order
#|   of magnitude in error. How to read this: the ordering within a panel is
#|   the benchmark result; the level across panels reflects how hard each
#|   split is (few geometries, or a single angle), not architecture. Float32.
#|   Data: as @tbl-scoreboard-surface.
#| code-fold: true
REF_KEYS = ["hl35", "hl210", "geo4", "geo21", "fixed", "dr435", "dr435_strat", "corner"]  # rungs where ISLA is measured
keys = REF_KEYS
short = {"hl35": "HiLift, 35 cases", "hl210": "HiLift, 210 cases",
         "geo4": "HiLift, 4 geometries", "geo21": "HiLift, 21 geometries", "fixed": "HiLift, fixed angle", "dr435": "DrivAerML, 435 cars",
         "dr435_strat": "DrivAerML, stratified draw", "corner": "DrivAerML, 512 × 80k"}
fig, axs = plt.subplots(2, 4, figsize=(12.0, 6.0))
axs = axs.ravel()
for ax, key in zip(axs, keys):
    s = S[key]
    arms = [("Geo-\nTransolver", s["gt"], "gt"), ("Transolver", s["t"], "t"), ("ISLA\nreference", s["isla_ref"], "isla_ref")]
    xs = list(range(len(arms))); means = [mean(v) for _, v, _ in arms]
    for x_, (_, v, k) in zip(xs, arms):
        ax.bar(x_, mean(v), width=0.62, zorder=2, **bar_kwargs(k))
        if len(v) > 1:
            ax.plot([x_] * len(v), v, marker="o", ms=4, mfc="white", mec=INK, mew=0.9, ls="none", zorder=4)
        ax.text(x_, mean(v) * 1.02, f"{mean(v):.3f}", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=7.5, color=INK2)
    ax.set_xticks(xs); ax.set_xticklabels([n for n, _, _ in arms], fontsize=7.5)
    ax.set_title(short[key], fontsize=9.5)
    ax.set_ylim(0, max(means) * 1.28); ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
    ax.tick_params(axis="y", labelsize=8)
axs[0].set_ylabel("surface pressure error [–]"); axs[4].set_ylabel("surface pressure error [–]")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-surface
#| output: asis
def fmt(v):
    if not v: return "pending"
    return f"{mean(v):.4f}" + (" (" + " / ".join(f"{x:.4f}" for x in v) + ")" if len(v) > 1 else "")
def rat(b, s):
    return f"**{ratio(b, s['isla_ref']):.2f}**" if b else "pending"
out = ("| setting | GeoTransolver | Transolver | ISLA | GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA | Transolver ÷ ISLA | validation cases where the baseline is lower |\n"
       "|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|\n")
for key in REF_KEYS:
    s = S[key]
    out += (f"| {s['title']} | {fmt(s['gt'])} | {fmt(s['t'])} | **{fmt(s['isla_ref'])}** "
            f"| {rat(s['gt'], s)} | {rat(s['t'], s)} | {s['paired'][0]} |\n")
print(out)
print(": Surface-pressure error (area-weighted relative L2, float32, final-epoch checkpoints; seed "
      "values in parentheses, the corner row lists seed means of two seeds) on every rung where the "
      "unit-direction baselines and ISLA are both measured. The ratio columns "
      "give baseline ÷ ISLA (above one favors ISLA). "
      "The corner row is width 512 and 80,000 cells per car for all arms (60.2M, 35.9M and 23.9M "
      "parameters), evaluated at 80,000 cells; ISLA there trained at the width "
      "learning rate 3.75e-4 (@sec-using-lr), the other arms at their protocol rates. The "
      "stratified-draw row queries the same 435-car checkpoints with a systematic sample along the Morton "
      "order of the cells, the inference sampler of @sec-using-sampler; the independent-draw rows are the "
      "book's headline ratios. Data: "
      + "; ".join(sorted({S[k]['src'] for k in REF_KEYS})) + ". {#tbl-scoreboard-surface}")
```

The DrivAerML gap at the reference size has a measured anatomy, about half of it finite-sample noise that the stratified draw or more cells removes (@sec-deficit-anatomy); the larger gaps at 35 wing cases are a different mechanism, the mesher-pattern cue where validation geometries recur in training (@sec-full-data).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Two configurations that are deliberately not rows"}
The baselines with ISLA's measure-weighted pooling, ablations that carry the same
quadrature measure in their slice pooling that ISLA does, keep the lead: at
35 wing cases they score
`{python} f"{mean(S['hl35']['gt_mw']):.3f}"` and
`{python} f"{mean(S['hl35']['t_mw']):.3f}"` (three seeds each; a
`{python} f"{(mean(S['hl35']['gt_mw'])/mean(S['hl35']['gt'])-1)*100:.0f}"` to
`{python} f"{(mean(S['hl35']['t_mw'])/mean(S['hl35']['t'])-1)*100:.0f}%"` price for the measure against
their unit-direction counterparts) against ISLA's
`{python} f"{mean(S['hl35']['isla_ref']):.3f}"`, and on DrivAerML
`{python} f"{mean(S['dr435']['gt_mw']):.4f}"` and
`{python} f"{mean(S['dr435']['t_mw']):.4f}"` at no price against
`{python} f"{mean(S['dr435']['isla_ref']):.4f}"`. The ISLA weights-off
ablation is not a row because it is not a configuration the program adopts:
it closes a third to all of the gap on the wing rungs by reading the
mesher's cell pattern, and under a change of sampling it collapses hardest
of every configuration measured (@sec-scoreboard-consistency,
@sec-limits-mechanism).
:::

### The sealed deflection split {#sec-scoreboard-other}

**Across a sealed geometry boundary both architectures degrade by the same
factor and the in-regime ordering carries through.** @tbl-scoreboard-other
holds the one surface setting that does not fit the ladder above: the wing
deflection split, which trains on the 80% of geometries with the milder
flap-and-slat settings and evaluates once, sealed, on the 20% most
aggressive (@sec-limits-regime).


## Interior fields from the surface {#sec-scoreboard-interior}

**On the boundary-to-interior task ISLA, with its
interior queries admitted as interacting tokens and given the signed
distance to the wall, is 27% more accurate than GeoTransolver's volume
configuration on interior velocity at a third of the parameters, 7% less
accurate on interior pressure and 14% less accurate on eddy viscosity.** The
task, the two architectures' interior modes and the diagnostics are in
@sec-interior; the numbers are in @fig-scoreboard-interior and
@tbl-scoreboard-interior. The interacting decode's prediction at a point
depends on the joint query set, so every interior value holds at the
training count of 10,000 queries, which is the deployment count
(@sec-interior-companion).

```{python}
#| label: fig-scoreboard-interior
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Interior error on the 48 DrivAerML validation cars for the three
#|   interior fields (panels), 10,000 interior queries per car, float32, two
#|   seeds (dots). Red: GeoTransolver-volume (27.6M parameters, unit
#|   direction). Blue: ISLA (query tokens
#|   with the signed distance, relative frame, total-measure length unit as
#|   trained, Horvitz–Thompson-corrected boundary measure; 8.9M). The
#|   label above the ISLA bar is GeoTransolver-volume's error divided by
#|   ISLA's (above 1 favors ISLA). How to read this: the arms receive
#|   the same per-point geometry (signed distance and its gradient) and
#|   differ in how the query consumes it and in width (ISLA has a third of
#|   the parameters; a parameter-matched ISLA exists only for the
#|   similarity-gauge variant, in the diagnostic note below). The values hold
#|   at the training count of 10,000 queries
#|   (@sec-interior-companion). Data: results/relint2_reduction_2026-09-14.json;
#|   results/fp32_reeval/fp32_shift_interior_2026-09-09.json.
#| code-fold: true
fields = [("pressure_l2", "interior pressure"), ("velocity_l2", "interior velocity"), ("nut_l2", "eddy viscosity")]
h344 = campD["isla_qtsdf_h344"]["per_seed"]  # similarity-gauge variant at width 344; diagnostic note only
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(10.0, 4.3))
for ax, (f, name) in zip(axs, fields):

            ("ISLA\n8.9M", ri2["relint2"][f]["seeds"], "isla_ref")]

    for x_, (_, v, k) in enumerate(arms):

        lab = f"{means[x_]:.4f}" + (f"\n÷ {means[0]/means[x_]:.2f}" if x_ else "")
        ax.text(x_, means[x_] * 1.02, lab, ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=8.5, color=INK2)
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(arms))); ax.set_xticklabels([n for n, _, _ in arms], fontsize=7.5)
    ax.set_title(name, fontsize=10); ax.set_ylim(0, max(means) * 1.32)
    ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
axs[0].set_ylabel("relative L2 over 48 cars [–]")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-interior
#| output: asis
def row(label, vals, ref=None):
    cells = []
    for f, _ in fields:
        m = mean(vals[f]); cells.append(f"{m:.4f}" + (f" ({mean(ref[f])/m:.2f})" if ref else ""))
    return f"| {label} | " + " | ".join(cells) + " |\n"
gtd = {f: fp(fpint, gtv, f) for f, _ in fields}
rfd = {f: ri2["relint2"][f]["seeds"] for f, _ in fields}
isd = {f: fp(fpint, isq, f) for f, _ in fields}
h3 = {f: [h344[s][f] for s in ("42", "43")] for f, _ in fields}
out = "| arm, 435 training cars | pressure | velocity | eddy viscosity |\n|---|---|---|---|\n"
out += row("GeoTransolver-volume, 27.6M, unit direction", gtd)
out += row("ISLA, query tokens + signed distance, 8.9M (GeoTransolver-volume ÷ ISLA)", rfd, gtd)
print(out)
print(": Interior error (relative L2 over the 48 DrivAerML validation cars, float32, two seeds, 10,000 "
      "interior queries per car, 500 epochs, learning rate 1e-3 for both arms). Ratios in parentheses are "
      "GeoTransolver-volume ÷ ISLA (above 1 favors ISLA). ISLA "
      "reads a 10,000-cell boundary sample with the Horvitz–Thompson-corrected measure. "
      "Data: results/relint2_reduction_2026-09-14.json; "
      "results/fp32_reeval/fp32_shift_interior_2026-09-09.json. "
      "{#tbl-scoreboard-interior}")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Interior rows measured only on the similarity-gauge variant (diagnostic): the parameter-matched width and the rungs below full data"}
The interior program was built on the similarity-gauge variant (measure-weighted
centroid and RMS-radius length unit) before the relative frame replaced it; the
variant reads a center estimated from the sample, so it appears only here. Two of
its measurements have no ISLA twin yet: the width-344 arm that matches
GeoTransolver-volume's 27.6M parameters, and the 54- and 109-car rungs. At
435 cars ISLA matches the variant on interior pressure and velocity (1.000x
and 0.991x) and is 12% more accurate on eddy viscosity
(results/relint2_reduction_2026-09-14.json), and on the surface the price of
not being told the body's center is at most about 2%, inside seed noise
(SG-REF, @sec-nb-sgref-verdict), so these trends are expected to carry to
ISLA; they are not rows until measured on it.

```{python}

    i = {f: fp(fpint, [f"v0l_isla_qtsdfval_n{n}_seed{s}" for s in (42, 43)], f) for f, _ in fields}

      "The variant's arms read about 365 boundary cells, a difference measured to be immaterial "
```

## Arbitrary poses: where the contract earns accuracy {#sec-scoreboard-pose}

**When every training and validation case arrives in its own random
orientation, ISLA's error moves by 1.5% and the augmented baselines' rises
by 12% and 16%, which makes ISLA 12% and 21% more accurate than
GeoTransolver and Transolver on the same posed cars at the reporting
protocol.** This is ISLA's one measured in-distribution accuracy lead over
input-matched baselines on the surface, and it is conditional on the
setting: in a canonical frame GeoTransolver is at parity
(@sec-scoreboard-200k), and GeoTransolver trained in a canonicalized frame
is pose-invariant at a 1% cost (@sec-pose). ISLA's rotation and translation
covariance is exact by construction (@sec-mt2-contracts) and needs no
augmentation; the same checkpoints scored in the native frame land within
0.5% of their posed numbers (@sec-nb-poseref-verdict). At the exploration
budget the lead was 7% and 17% (the second table below).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-pose-200k
#| output: asis
PP = J("p200k_pose_reduction_2026-09-19.json"); NAT = PP["native_frame_reference"]
def seeds2(a): return " / ".join(f"{v['pressure_l2']:.4f}" for v in a["per_seed"].values())
out = "| architecture | native frame | every case in a random pose | posed ÷ native | baseline ÷ ISLA, posed |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n"
for label, key in (("GeoTransolver, trained with rotation augmentation (native at 1e-3)", "gt_unit"), ("Transolver, trained with rotation augmentation", "transolver_unit"), ("ISLA, no augmentation", "isla")):
    a = PP["arms"][key]
    out += f"| {label} | {NAT[key]:.4f} | {a['posed_mean']:.4f} ({seeds2(a)}) | {a['posed_over_native']:.3f} | {a['posed_mean']/PP['arms']['isla']['posed_mean']:.2f} |\n"
print(out)
print(": The pose test at the reporting protocol: DrivAerML surface pressure, 435 training cars, 48 validation cars, 200,000 cells, float32, two seeds each. "
      "The native column is each architecture's error in the dataset's frame from @tbl-scoreboard-200k (GeoTransolver's posed lanes ran at 1e-3, so its native reference here is the 1e-3 pair); the posed column trains and validates with every case rotated by its own random rotation. "
      "Data: results/p200k_pose_reduction_2026-09-19.json; results/p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json. {#tbl-scoreboard-pose-200k}")
```

## Consistency under a change of surface sampling {#sec-scoreboard-consistency}

**Every configuration that centers its coordinates on a statistic of the
sampled points, whichever architecture it belongs to, degrades 10 to 16x
when the same surface is resampled with a 10:1 front-to-back density bias;
frames that read nothing from the sample hold at 1.1 to 1.2x, and the
baselines join that group once their datapipe centers on an unbiased
estimate of the geometric centroid.** Consistency in the fine-mesh limit is
the acceptance criterion of @sec-principle, not a score: a model whose
prediction depends on where the mesher happened to refine is not predicting
the physics. The probe holds the geometry fixed and redraws 10,000 cells
with the bias, with exact Horvitz–Thompson weights so a measure-consistent
model sees the same surface integral; the ratio of the error under the
biased draw to the error under the uniform draw is the number in
@fig-scoreboard-density, stated in the sample frame, the frame a biased
mesher would deliver.

```{python}
#| label: fig-scoreboard-density
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Sampling-density sensitivity by configuration on DrivAerML (48 cars,
#|   10,000 cells, float32, two or three seeds): surface-pressure error under
#|   the 10:1 front/back biased draw divided by the same checkpoint's error
#|   under the uniform draw, on a log axis; 1 is exact consistency and the
#|   gray band marks up to 1.5x. Bars are sample-frame values, in which every
#|   model's input is centered on the drawn points. Open markers on the
#|   baseline rows are the same checkpoints with the frame handed to them
#|   unbiased by the pipeline (pool frame); the two rows marked "HT-centered
#|   datapipe" are baselines retrained with the datapipe centering on the
#|   Horvitz–Thompson estimate of the geometric centroid. Color follows the
#|   book's key: ISLA blue,
#|   GeoTransolver red, Transolver amber, ablations in the lighter
#|   tints. How to read this: a bar near 1 means the configuration's
#|   answer does not depend on the sampling law at this count; it does not
#|   rank in-distribution accuracy, which is in @tbl-scoreboard-surface. Data:
#|   results/accuracy_consistency_matrix_2026-09-10.json (provenance per cell
#|   inside) and results/mwaw_2026-09-11.json.
#| code-fold: true
R = MAT["rows"]
items = [  # (label, sample-frame factor, pool-frame factor or None, style key)
    ("ISLA", R["isla_relative_frame_meas"]["density_factor"], None, "isla_ref"),
    ("GeoTransolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling + HT-centered datapipe (ablation)", mwaw["runs"]["mwaw_dr_gt_unit_lr1e3"]["probe_sfht"]["ratio_mean"], None, "gt_var"),
    ("Transolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling + HT-centered datapipe (ablation)", mwaw["runs"]["mwaw_dr_transolver_unit_lr3e3"]["probe_sfht"]["ratio_mean"], None, "t_var"),
    ("GeoTransolver", R["geotransolver_unit"]["density_factor"], R["geotransolver_unit"]["density_factor_pipeline_frame"], "gt"),
    ("Transolver", R["transolver_unit"]["density_factor"], R["transolver_unit"]["density_factor_pipeline_frame"], "t"),
    ("GeoTransolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling (ablation)", R["geotransolver_unit_mw"]["density_factor"], R["geotransolver_unit_mw"]["density_factor_pipeline_frame"], "gt_var"),
    ("Transolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling (ablation)", R["transolver_unit_mw"]["density_factor"], R["transolver_unit_mw"]["density_factor_pipeline_frame"], "t_var"),
]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10.6, 4.6))
y = list(range(len(items)))[::-1]
ax.axvspan(1.0, 1.5, color=GRID, alpha=0.7, zorder=0)
for yy, (label, sf, pf, k) in zip(y, items):
    ax.barh(yy, sf, height=0.62, zorder=2, **bar_kwargs(k))
    ax.text(sf * 1.06, yy, f"{sf:.2f}x", va="center", fontsize=8.5, color=INK2)
    if pf:
        c = STYLE[k]["color"]
        ax.plot([pf], [yy], marker="o", ms=7, mfc="white", mec=c, mew=1.8, ls="none", zorder=4)
        ax.text(pf, yy + 0.36, f"pool frame {pf:.1f}x", ha="center", fontsize=7.5, color=c)
ax.set_yticks(y); ax.set_yticklabels([i[0] for i in items], fontsize=8.5)
ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_xlim(0.9, 45)
ax.set_xticks([1, 1.5, 2, 5, 10, 20]); ax.set_xticklabels(["1", "1.5", "2", "5", "10", "20"])
ax.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter())
ax.axvline(1.0, color=INK2, lw=1.0, zorder=1)
ax.set_xlabel("error under 10:1 biased sampling ÷ error under uniform sampling [–]\n(sample frame: each model's input frame taken from the drawn points)", fontsize=9.5)
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The single-count probe understates the question the principle asks, which
is whether the prediction converges to one field as the sample is refined
and to the same field under two sampling laws. The consistency benchmark of
@sec-consistency-bench evaluates every checkpoint at 2,500 to 40,000 cells
under three samplers; @tbl-scoreboard-bench reads it at 40,000 cells, where
a consistent configuration is within 3% of its own uniform-sampling answer.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-bench
#| output: asis
def bench(path): return J("consistency_bench/" + path)["arms"]
B0, Bmw, Bmc, Brf = (bench("consistency_bench_2026-09-10.json"), bench("consistency_bench_mw_2026-09-10.json"),
                     bench("consistency_bench_mcenter_2026-09-10.json"), bench("consistency_bench_rf_2026-09-11.json"))
def D(arms, arm, sampler, count="40000"):
    t = arms[arm]["table"]; return t[sampler][count]["pressure_l2"]["mean"] / t["unif"][count]["pressure_l2"]["mean"] - 1
def cell(arms, arm):
    return f"{D(arms, arm, 'area'):+.0%} / {D(arms, arm, 'biased'):+.0%}"
rows = [
    ("ISLA", "in-model, none", (Brf, "rf_dr_mt2_meas"), (Brf, "rf_hl_mt2_meas_super_scarce")),
    ("GeoTransolver", "pipeline pool mean (unbiased)", (B0, "uw_gt_unit_lr1e3"), (B0, "udrv_hl_gt_super_scarce_lr3e3")),
    ("Transolver", "pipeline pool mean (unbiased)", (B0, "uw_transolver_unit_lr3e3"), (B0, "udrv_hl_transolver_super_scarce_lr3e3")),
    ("GeoTransolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling (ablation)", "pipeline pool mean (unbiased)", (Bmw, "mw_dr_gt_unit_lr1e3"), (Bmw, "mw_hl_gt_super_scarce_lr3e3")),
    ("Transolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling (ablation)", "pipeline pool mean (unbiased)", (Bmw, "mw_dr_transolver_unit_lr3e3"), (Bmw, "mw_hl_transolver_super_scarce_lr3e3")),
]
out = "| configuration | frame convention in the benchmark | DrivAerML: area / biased | HiLift 35 cases: area / biased |\n|---|---|---:|---:|\n"
for label, frame, dr, hl in rows:
    out += f"| {label} | {frame} | {cell(*dr)} | {cell(*hl) if hl else 'not run'} |\n"
print(out)
print(": Sampling-distribution dependence at 40,000 cells, float32, two seeds: the change in "
      "surface-pressure error when the same surface is drawn proportionally to cell area (area) or "
      "with the 10:1 front/back bias (biased) instead of uniformly over cells, as a percentage of the "
      "uniform-draw error; within ±3% counts as consistent. The frame column states where each "
      "model's input frame came from in this benchmark: the baselines received their center from the "
      "pipeline's uniform 320,000-cell pool before the draw, an unbiased frame that a biased mesher "
      "would not deliver (their sample-frame sensitivity is the bar in @fig-scoreboard-density), while "
      "ISLA computes its frame in the model from the drawn points. With the frame held, measure "
      "weighting makes the baselines' aggregation consistent; the frame is the separate defect. Data: "
      "results/consistency_bench/consistency_bench_2026-09-10.json and its _mw and _rf "
      "companions. {#tbl-scoreboard-bench}")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="The legacy centered variant and the weights-off ablation under the same probes (diagnostic)"}
These rows establish one mechanism: a frame centered on the plain mean of
the sampled points collapses under a change of sampling law, and nothing
else in the model does, since the same checkpoint re-evaluated with a
measure-weighted center, or given the exact frame of the full geometry,
holds with ISLA.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-legacy-consistency
#| output: asis
legacy = [
    ("legacy centered variant (plain-mean center)", R["isla_reference_constant_gauge"]["density_factor"], (B0, "iw_mt2_lr1e3"), (B0, "lad_hl_mt2_super_scarce")),
    ("the same checkpoint with a measure-weighted center", R["isla_constant_gauge_mcenter"]["density_factor"], (Bmc, "cg_dr_mt2_mcenter"), (Bmc, "cg_hl_mt2_mcenter_super_scarce")),
    ("the same checkpoint given the exact full-geometry frame", R["isla_frame_full_frame"]["density_factor"], None, None),
    ("weights-off ablation (never adopted)", R["isla_weights_off_ablation"]["density_factor"], (B0, "now_mt2_lr1e3"), (B0, "a35_hl_mt2_noweights")),
]
out = "| configuration (diagnostic) | 10:1 density bias, sample frame: biased ÷ uniform | 40,000 cells, DrivAerML: area / biased | 40,000 cells, HiLift 35 cases: area / biased |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n"
for label, df, dr, hl in legacy:
    out += f"| {label} | {df:.2f}x | {cell(*dr) if dr else 'not run'} | {cell(*hl) if hl else 'not run'} |\n"
print(out)
print(": The legacy centered variant under the two consistency instruments of this section, and the "
      "weights-off ablation, which reads the mesher's cell pattern and collapses hardest of every "
      "configuration measured. Data: results/accuracy_consistency_matrix_2026-09-10.json; "
      "results/consistency_bench/consistency_bench_2026-09-10.json and its _mcenter companion. "
      "{#tbl-scoreboard-legacy-consistency}")
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="The similarity-gauge variant under the same probes (diagnostic)"}
The similarity-gauge variant centers on the measure-weighted centroid and
scales by the RMS radius, both integrals of the sampled geometry, so it is
consistent under a change of sampling law like ISLA; what it adds is a
center estimated from the sample, which ISLA declines on principle. Its
price, on the surface at 435 cars: the price of not being told the body's
center is at most about 2%, inside seed noise (SG-REF,
@sec-nb-sgref-verdict).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-sg-consistency
#| output: asis
sgc = [("similarity-gauge variant (lr 1e-3)", R["isla_similarity_gauge_lr1e3"]["density_factor"], None, None),
       ("similarity-gauge variant (lr 3e-3)", None, (B0, "iw_mt2_gauge"), None)]
out = "| configuration (diagnostic) | 10:1 density bias, sample frame: biased ÷ uniform | 40,000 cells, DrivAerML: area / biased | 40,000 cells, HiLift 35 cases: area / biased |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n"
for label, df, dr, hl in sgc:
    out += f"| {label} | {f'{df:.2f}x' if df else 'not run'} | {cell(*dr) if dr else 'not run'} | {cell(*hl) if hl else 'not run'} |\n"
print(out)
print(": The similarity-gauge variant under the two consistency instruments of this section. Data: "
      "results/accuracy_consistency_matrix_2026-09-10.json; "
      "results/consistency_bench/consistency_bench_2026-09-10.json. "
      "{#tbl-scoreboard-sg-consistency}")
```
:::

Read together, the two instruments say one thing: the sampling-law
dependence of every architecture at the reference size lives in the input
frame, not in the attention. Measure weighting in the slice pooling repairs
the aggregation for the Transolver family at no accuracy cost on DrivAerML
and at `{python} f"{(mean(S['hl35']['gt_mw'])/mean(S['hl35']['gt'])-1)*100:.0f}"` to
`{python} f"{(mean(S['hl35']['t_mw'])/mean(S['hl35']['t'])-1)*100:.0f}%"` on the wings at 35
cases; a frame that is a property of the geometry rather
than of the sample, whether ISLA's relative frame or a Horvitz–Thompson
centroid in the baselines' datapipe, removes the rest. The Horvitz–Thompson
centered baselines are ablations that locate the property; the
GeoTransolver and Transolver keep their plain-mean frame
(@sec-part-baseline), so the deployable comparison is the baselines
against ISLA.

A reader of @fig-scoreboard-density will ask why one would not simply use
GeoTransolver with ISLA's measure-weighted pooling and the
Horvitz–Thompson-centered datapipe. One could, and the figure is the
evidence that consistency under a change of sampling is not ISLA's property
alone: it belongs to two choices any slice-attention model can make, the
measure in the pooling and a frame taken from integrals of the surface. The
ablation pays little for them in distribution (its uniform-draw error is
`{python} f"{mean(mwaw['runs']['mwaw_dr_gt_unit_lr1e3']['probe_sfht']['unif']):.4f}"`
against GeoTransolver's
`{python} f"{mean(S['dr435']['gt']):.4f}"`), and under the refinement
benchmark it is consistent at every count, and more consistent than ISLA
(@tbl-scoreboard-steelman). What it buys consistency with is a body
centroid: the datapipe centers every coordinate on the measure-weighted
centroid of the surface, a point the physics does not distinguish and that
is ill-posed for an open, truncated or multi-body boundary, and the model
then consumes absolute positions in that frame in every layer. That is the
construct ISLA declines (@sec-mt2-variants). It also does not make the
model covariant: its pose behavior still comes from augmentation or a
canonical frame. The comparison the book makes is therefore not "consistent
against inconsistent" but "consistent and exactly covariant without any
centroid, at a measured price in distribution" against "consistent with a
centroid, position-informed, not covariant".

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-steelman
#| output: asis
SM = J("steelman_reduction_2026-09-18.json")["arms"]
RFB = J("consistency_bench/consistency_bench_rf_2026-09-11.json")["arms"]["rf_dr_mt2_meas"]["table"]
def dev(arm, s, c): return SM[arm]["deviation_over_unif"][s][str(c)]["mean"]
out = "| model | uniform error, 10,000 cells | area ÷ uniform at 2,500 / 10,000 / 40,000 | biased ÷ uniform at 2,500 / 10,000 / 40,000 |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n"
for arm, lab in (("gt_ht", "GeoTransolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling + HT-centered datapipe (ablation)"), ("t_ht", "Transolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling + HT-centered datapipe (ablation)")):
    out += f"| {lab} | {SM[arm]['table']['unif']['10000']['mean']:.4f} | " + " / ".join(f"{dev(arm,'area',c):.3f}" for c in (2500, 10000, 40000)) + " | " + " / ".join(f"{dev(arm,'biased',c):.3f}" for c in (2500, 10000, 40000)) + " |\n"
isla_u = {c: RFB["unif"][c]["pressure_l2"]["mean"] for c in ("10000", "40000")}
out += (f"| ISLA | {isla_u['10000']:.4f} | — / {RFB['area']['10000']['pressure_l2']['mean']/isla_u['10000']:.3f} / {RFB['area']['40000']['pressure_l2']['mean']/isla_u['40000']:.3f} "
        f"| — / {RFB['biased']['10000']['pressure_l2']['mean']/isla_u['10000']:.3f} / {RFB['biased']['40000']['pressure_l2']['mean']/isla_u['40000']:.3f} |\n")
print(out)
print(": The steel-man of the consistency claim: the two baseline ablations that adopt ISLA's measure semantics and an "
      "integral (Horvitz–Thompson) centroid, through the refinement benchmark (float32, 48 DrivAerML validation cars, "
      "two seeds each, seed means), with ISLA on the same benchmark for context. A deviation of 1.000 is exact consistency; "
      "the benchmark's bar is 3% at 40,000 cells. How to read this: the ablations are consistent at every count and more "
      "consistent than ISLA; the comparison ISLA makes is covariance and center-freeness on top of consistency, not "
      "consistency alone. ISLA's 2,500-cell row is not in its benchmark artifact. Data: results/steelman_reduction_2026-09-18.json; "
      "results/consistency_bench/consistency_bench_rf_2026-09-11.json. {#tbl-scoreboard-steelman}")
```

On the wings the relative frame's
convergence is measured on the fixed-angle split: from 2,500 to 40,000 cells
its area-sampler deviation falls from +45% to +2.6% and its biased-sampler
deviation from +81% to +5.5%, converging but not yet at the bias bar at
40,000, while it is the most accurate ISLA arm under every sampler at every
count (@sec-consistency-bench).

## Resources behind the comparison {#sec-scoreboard-resources}

**The three architectures are parameter-matched at the reference width, and
ISLA trains in the least memory once its geometry is recomputed in the
backward pass.** @tbl-scoreboard-resources measures the eager path on which
all three can be run on one instrument; on the compiled path the recipe
runs, ISLA's training step is 1.05x GeoTransolver's at 10,000 tokens with
the recompute on and 0.86x without, at half the memory (@sec-mt2-cost).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-resources
#| output: asis
def cfg(name, tokens):
    return next(c for c in cost["configs"] if c["name"] == name and c["tokens"] == tokens)
rows = [("ISLA, hidden 192", "isla_h192_fast_plain"),
        ("ISLA, hidden 192, geometry recomputed in the backward pass (the recipe's default)", "isla_h192_fast_ckpt"),
        ("GeoTransolver, hidden 256", "gt_h256"),
        ("Transolver, hidden 256", "transolver_h256")]
out = "| configuration | parameters | step at 10,000 tokens [ms] | peak memory at 10,000 tokens [GiB] | step at 80,000 tokens [ms] | peak memory at 80,000 tokens [GiB] |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n"
for label, name in rows:
    a, b = cfg(name, 10000), cfg(name, 80000)
    out += (f"| {label} | {a['n_params']/1e6:.1f}M | {statistics.median(a['step_ms']):.0f} | {max(a['incremental_peak_allocated_bytes'])/2**30:.2f} "
            f"| {statistics.median(b['step_ms']):.0f} | {max(b['incremental_peak_allocated_bytes'])/2**30:.1f} |\n")
print(out)
print(": Training cost of the three architectures on one instrument and one execution path: one "
      "GB300 GPU, eager execution, batch of one case, bfloat16 autocast, AdamW step, median of five "
      "measured steps after three warm-up steps; memory is the peak allocated during the step net of "
      "the resident parameters and optimizer state. The recomputed-geometry row is the same function at "
      "a lower memory and a higher step time. The compiled path the recipe trains on is in @tbl-mt2-cost. "
      "Data: results/isla_vs_baselines_cost_fastkernel_2026-09-09.json. {#tbl-scoreboard-resources}")
```

The token budget decides the cost comparison more than the architecture
does. @fig-cost-sweep sweeps the training step from 2,500 to 200,000 tokens
per case on the compiled path every model trains on. GeoTransolver's step is
nearly flat below 40,000 tokens, where the GPU is not saturated, and grows
to about twice its 10,000-token value at the recipe's default of 200,000;
ISLA on its default path (geometry recomputed in the backward pass) grows
linearly from 20,000 tokens on and is five times GeoTransolver's step at
200,000, while ISLA with the fused geometry kernel tracks GeoTransolver's
step at every count in less than half its memory. At the recipe default of
200,000 cells every model fits one GB300 with room to spare; GeoTransolver's
49 GiB would not fit an 80 GB card.

```{python}
#| label: fig-cost-sweep
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Training-step time (top) and peak allocated memory (bottom) against the
#|   number of tokens per case, one GB300, bf16 autocast, batch of one case,
#|   AdamW step included, every model compiled, median of ten measured steps
#|   after warm-up on random inputs. ISLA is shown on its recipe-default path
#|   (geometry recomputed in the backward pass) and with the opt-in fused
#|   geometry kernel (open squares, dashed). How to read this: the two axes
#|   are logarithmic and the lines are joined measurements, not fits; the
#|   sweep measures the step alone, and the training lanes of this book are
#|   dominated by data loading, so it ranks the models' step cost, not their
#|   wall-clock. The 200,000-token column is the recipe's default budget.
#|   Data: results/cost_sweep_gb300_bf16_2026-09-18.json.
#| code-fold: true
import statistics as st
CS = J("cost_sweep_gb300_bf16_2026-09-18.json")["runs"]
arms = [("isla_compiled_recompute", "isla_ref", "ISLA (recipe default path)", {}),
        ("isla_fused_compiled", "isla_ref", "ISLA + fused geometry kernel", dict(ls="--", mfc="white")),
        ("geotransolver_compiled", "gt", "GeoTransolver", {}),
        ("transolver_compiled", "t", "Transolver", {})]
fig, (ax0, ax1) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8.0, 6.6), sharex=True, gridspec_kw=dict(hspace=0.08))
for arm, key, lab, ov in arms:
    rows = sorted([r for r in CS if r["arm"] == arm and r["status"] == "ok"], key=lambda r: r["tokens"])
    xs = [r["tokens"] for r in rows]
    ax0.plot(xs, [st.median(r["step_ms"]) for r in rows], **series_kwargs(key, label=lab, **ov))
    ax1.plot(xs, [r["peak_allocated_gib"] for r in rows], **series_kwargs(key, label=lab, **ov))
for ax in (ax0, ax1):
    ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_yscale("log"); ax.grid(True, which="major", color=GRID); ax.grid(False, which="minor")
ax0.set_ylabel("training step [ms]"); ax1.set_ylabel("peak allocated memory [GiB]")
ax0.set_yticks([20, 50, 100, 200, 500]); ax0.set_yticklabels(["20", "50", "100", "200", "500"])
ax1.set_yticks([0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50]); ax1.set_yticklabels(["0.5", "1", "2", "5", "10", "20", "50"])
ax1.set_xticks([2500, 10000, 40000, 80000, 200000]); ax1.set_xticklabels(["2,500", "10,000", "40,000", "80,000", "200,000"])
ax1.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter()); ax0.yaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter()); ax1.yaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter())
ax1.set_xlabel("tokens per case [count]")
ax1.axvline(200000, color=BASELINE, lw=1.0, zorder=0); ax0.axvline(200000, color=BASELINE, lw=1.0, zorder=0)
ax0.text(200000, ax0.get_ylim()[1] * 0.9, " recipe default", fontsize=8, color=INK2, va="top")
ax0.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=8.5)
ax0.set_title("training-step cost against token count, one GB300, bf16, batch 1, compiled")
plt.show()
```

## The standing against the token budget {#sec-scoreboard-tokens}

**The DrivAerML in-distribution gap was a property of the 10,000-cell
budget: it closes to parity at the recipe default.** The rows of
@sec-scoreboard-surface train and score at 10,000 sampled cells per case,
the program's exploration count. Trained and scored at 40,000 and 80,000
cells at the same width, the baselines improve by 8% and ISLA by 16%, and
the ratio moves from 0.90 to 0.985 against GeoTransolver and past parity
against Transolver (@tbl-scoreboard-tokens); at the reporting protocol of
200,000 cells, each architecture at its own best rate, GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA
is 0.998 (@sec-scoreboard-200k). The ISLA in the 40,000- and 80,000-cell
rows is the legacy centered variant, the only ISLA trained at those counts;
its 10,000-cell value is within 1% of ISLA's on this dataset, so the ratios
read across.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-tokens
#| output: asis
TP = J("tokproto_reduction_2026-09-18.json")
r10 = TP["ratios_10k"]
out = "| cells per case (train and score) | GeoTransolver | Transolver | ISLA (legacy centered variant) | GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA | Transolver ÷ ISLA |\n|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n"
out += f"| 10,000 | {mean(S['dr435']['gt']):.4f} | {mean(S['dr435']['t']):.4f} | {mean(S['dr435']['isla_cg']) if 'isla_cg' in S['dr435'] and S['dr435']['isla_cg'] else 0.0558:.4f} | {r10['gt_over_isla']:.3f} | {r10['t_over_isla']:.3f} |\n"
for c in ("40000", "80000"):
    t = TP["table"][c]
    sd = lambda k: " / ".join(f"{v:.4f}" for v in t[k]["seeds"])
    out += f"| {int(c):,} | {t['gt']['mean']:.4f} ({sd('gt')}) | {t['t']['mean']:.4f} ({sd('t')}) | {t['isla_cg']['mean']:.4f} ({sd('isla_cg')}) | {t['gt_over_isla']:.3f} | {t['t_over_isla']:.3f} |\n"
print(out)
print(": Surface-pressure error (area-weighted relative L2, float32, 48 DrivAerML validation cars, 435 training cars, "
      "width 192) when every model trains and is scored at the same cell count, seed means with the two seeds in "
      "parentheses. ISLA is the legacy centered variant at 40,000 and 80,000 cells (the only ISLA trained there) and at "
      "10,000 for like-for-like. How to read this: the ratio moves toward and past parity with the budget; it does not "
      "show the recipe default of 200,000 cells, where the reporting lanes are training. Data: "
      "results/tokproto_reduction_2026-09-18.json; results/fp32_reeval/fp32_shift_drivaer_2026-09-09.json. {#tbl-scoreboard-tokens}")
```

## The standing at the reporting protocol: 200,000 cells {#sec-scoreboard-200k}

**At the reporting protocol, the recipe's default of 200,000 sampled cells
per case, ISLA and GeoTransolver are at parity on DrivAerML at full data
(0.998), ISLA leads Transolver by 6%, and below full data GeoTransolver
holds a data-efficiency lead that narrows from 17% at 27 cars to zero at
435.** This is the book's primary standing on DrivAerML; the 10,000-cell
rows of @sec-scoreboard-surface are the exploration budget. The table is
computed from the 200,000-cell artifacts and names GeoTransolver's rate on
every row, because GeoTransolver's best rate depends on how much data it
sees: 3e-3 beats 1e-3 by 31%, 24%, 10%, 4% and 2% at 27, 54, 109, 218 and
435 cars at this budget, where 1e-3 had won its 435-car grid at 10,000
cells (@sec-nb-rategt-prereg, @sec-nb-proto200k-verdict). ISLA has one
usable rate (1e-3 at width 192; @sec-robustness-lr) and Transolver runs at
3e-3 throughout. A row would mark itself *provisional* if a rate control
were still training; none is.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scoreboard-200k
#| output: asis
P2 = J("p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json"); L2 = J("p200k_ladder_interim_2026-09-18.json")
def cell(a): return (f"{a['pressure_mean']:.4f}", " / ".join(f"{v['pressure_l2']:.4f}" for v in a["per_seed"].values())) if a and a.get("pressure_mean") else None
out = "| DrivAerML training cars | ISLA (1e-3) | GeoTransolver (better of 1e-3, 3e-3) | Transolver (3e-3) | GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA | Transolver ÷ ISLA | status |\n|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|\n"
for n in ("n27", "n54", "n109", "n218"):
    r = L2["rungs"][n]; isla = r["isla"]["pressure_mean"]; g1 = r["gt_unit"]
    rc = r.get("rate_control_lr3e3", {}).get("gt_unit_lr3e3")
    if rc and rc["pressure_mean"] < g1["pressure_mean"]:
        g, glab, status = rc, "3e-3", "final"
    elif rc:
        g, glab, status = g1, "1e-3", "final"
    else:
        g, glab, status = g1, "1e-3", "provisional: 3e-3 control training"
    t = r["transolver_unit"]
    out += (f"| {n[1:]} | {isla:.4f} | {g['pressure_mean']:.4f} ({glab}) | {t['pressure_mean']:.4f} | {g['pressure_mean']/isla:.2f} | {t['pressure_mean']/isla:.2f} | {status} |\n")
A = P2["arms"]; isla = A["isla"]["pressure_mean"]
gts = {k: A[k]["pressure_mean"] for k in ("gt_unit_lr1e3", "gt_unit_lr3e3") if A[k]["pressure_mean"] and A[k]["n"] == 2}
best = min(gts, key=gts.get); glab = "3e-3" if best.endswith("3e3") else "1e-3"
status = "final" if "gt_unit_lr3e3" in gts else "provisional: 3e-3 control training"
out += (f"| **435** | **{isla:.4f}** | **{gts[best]:.4f}** ({glab}) | **{A['transolver_unit_lr3e3']['pressure_mean']:.4f}** | **{gts[best]/isla:.2f}** | **{A['transolver_unit_lr3e3']['pressure_mean']/isla:.2f}** | {status} |\n")
print(out)
print(": Surface-pressure error (area-weighted relative L2, float32, 48 DrivAerML validation cars) with every model trained and "
      "scored at 200,000 sampled cells per case, width 192, 500 epochs, two seeds (seed means; the per-seed values are in the "
      "artifacts). GeoTransolver's column takes the better of its 1e-3 and 3e-3 pairs and names the rate; a row marked provisional "
      "still awaits that control. ISLA carries the total-measure length unit in these lanes (the RMS-pairwise-distance unit, now "
      "the default, is within 1.3% of it, @sec-nb-lenrms-verdict). How to read this: ratios above 1 favor ISLA; the 10,000-cell "
      "rows elsewhere in this chapter are the exploration budget and are not comparable in absolute value. Data: "
      "results/p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json; results/p200k_ladder_interim_2026-09-18.json. {#tbl-scoreboard-200k}")
```

```{python}
#| label: para-200k-reading
#| output: asis
gt_final = "gt_unit_lr3e3" in gts
r435 = gts[best] / isla; t435 = A["transolver_unit_lr3e3"]["pressure_mean"] / isla
standing = "at parity with" if abs(r435 - 1) < 0.01 else ("ahead of" if r435 > 1 else "behind")
lads = [L2["rungs"][n]["gt_over_isla_at_better_rates"] for n in ("n27", "n54", "n109", "n218")]
print(f"At 435 cars ISLA is {standing} GeoTransolver (GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA {r435:.3f}, GeoTransolver at {glab}) and leads Transolver by {(t435-1)*100:.0f}%"
      f"{'' if gt_final else '; GeoTransolver’s 3e-3 pair is still training and the row is provisional'}. "
      f"Against the 10,000-cell standings (@sec-scoreboard-surface) every model improved, ISLA by the most "
      f"({(1-P2['verdict']['isla_200k_over_10k'])*100:.0f}% against {(1-gts[best]/0.0503)*100:.0f}% for GeoTransolver and "
      f"{(1-A['transolver_unit_lr3e3']['pressure_mean']/0.0517)*100:.0f}% for Transolver), which is the count-noise term of the deficit anatomy "
      f"(@sec-deficit-anatomy) going to zero at the denser sampling. Below full data GeoTransolver at its better rate "
      f"leads ISLA by {', '.join(f'{(1-r)*100:.0f}%' for r in lads)} at 27, 54, 109 and 218 cars: the data-efficiency ordering of the "
      f"10,000-cell ladder survives the change of budget with a smaller gap at every rung, and closes at the full training set. "
      f"On the wings the budget changes nothing: on the 35-case rung GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA is 0.73 at 200,000 cells against 0.72 at 10,000 "
      f"(@tbl-scoreboard-200k-wings), so that deficit is a property of the trained functions, not of the sampling count.")
```

## What is not yet on the board {#sec-scoreboard-pending}

Five measurements would complete the board, and one line is closed; the
live status of each is in @sec-program-status.

- **ISLA on 510 and 1,260 wing cases**: not yet
  measured. The unit-direction baselines' values on those rungs are in
  results/udrvl_510_reduction_2026-09-12.json,
  results/udrv_1260_reduction_2026-09-15.json and
  results/udrv_1260_transolver_2026-09-16.json.
- **The remaining wing rungs at the reporting protocol.** The 35-case rung
  is measured at 200,000 cells (@tbl-scoreboard-200k-wings); the 105-,
  510- and 1,260-case rungs, the geometry ladders and the fixed angle are
  training at that budget (@sec-program-status).
- **ISLA below full data on the DrivAerML interior ladder**, measured only
  on a variant that this chapter reports in a diagnostic note
  (@tbl-scoreboard-interior-sg); the surface ladder is measured on ISLA at
  the reporting protocol (@tbl-scoreboard-200k).
- **The baselines' consistency with a Horvitz–Thompson centroid on the
  wings.** It is measured on DrivAerML only, and only as a ablation.
- **Multi-head slice routing at 435 cars.** On a one-car instrument eight
  independent routings per block lowered ISLA's floor by 19%; the run at the
  full training set is in progress (@sec-nb-heads435-prereg).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="The closed line: oversampling the far wake"}
The far-wake deficit carries ISLA's interior eddy-viscosity gap. The one
remedy tested, oversampling the far field in the interior training queries
with exact measure weights, makes every field worse. Trained that way and
scored on the standard uniform interior sample, the arm is worse than the
similarity-gauge interior variant (diagnostic) it was built from on every field and in
every wall-distance band (pressure, velocity and eddy viscosity
`{python} f"{fw['two_seed_mean']['pressure_l2']/fw['reference_three_seed_fp32']['pressure_l2']-1:+.0%}"`,
`{python} f"{fw['two_seed_mean']['velocity_l2']/fw['reference_three_seed_fp32']['velocity_l2']-1:+.0%}"` and
`{python} f"{fw['two_seed_mean']['nut_l2']/fw['reference_three_seed_fp32']['nut_l2']-1:+.0%}"`;
far-shell eddy viscosity beyond 0.4 body lengths
`{python} f"{fs['isla_farwake']['mean']['nut']['>=0.4L']['rel_l2']:.3f}"` against
`{python} f"{fs['isla_ref']['mean']['nut']['>=0.4L']['rel_l2']:.3f}"` for the
similarity-gauge variant and
`{python} f"{fs['gt_unit']['mean']['nut']['>=0.4L']['rel_l2']:.3f}"` for
GeoTransolver-volume; float32, two seeds,
results/farwake_reduction_2026-09-11.json and
results/farwake_far_field_shells_2026-09-11.json). The arm trains the
interacting decode on one query law and scores it on another, so it settles
the deployable question and not the mechanism, and it has no baseline twin,
which is why it is a closed line and not a row (@sec-interior-negatives).
:::

No row above depends on the weights-off ablation, on a bfloat16 evaluation,
or on a physical-velocity baseline, except where the caption says so.
